claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has superior tribo-corrosion resistance relative to duplex stainless steel 2205.
The superior tribo-corrosion resistance is governed by a stable dual-phase L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The L12/B2 lamellar microstructure produces a more homogeneous distribution of Cr.
Homogeneous Cr availability enables rapid and robust passive-film repair.
Passive-film repair maintains a cohesive, low-shear passive or compacted tribo-layer that suppresses debris-assisted wear.
Repassivation is optimized at approximately 50 °C.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 contains approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2 phases.
The B2 lamellae in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 are approximately 2–3 µm thick and contain nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates.
The duplex stainless steel 2205 baseline contains approximately 52% austenite and 48% ferrite.
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 lamellar microstructure remains intact and phase-stable through the stated thermal and tribo-corrosion treatment.
DS2205 undergoes phase redistribution and forms less mechanically stable films, leading to greater debris-assisted wear.
Temperature governs the balance between sliding-induced depassivation and thermally activated repassivation.
At 25 °C, slower passive-film repair promotes two-body abrasive wear.
At approximately 50 °C, fast and uniform passive-film repair without brittle oxide interruption produces a polishing wear regime.
At 100 °C, repeated oxide formation and removal destabilize the tribo-layer and promote third-body wear.
Under identical conditions, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will have lower wear volume and tribo-corrosion wear rate than DS2205.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit a lower and more stable coefficient of friction than DS2205.
Both alloys will show less degradation at 50 °C than at 25 °C or 100 °C.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will retain its phase structure and smaller wear-track dimensions better than DS2205.
The proposed mechanism applies over 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, and 3–9 Hz in low-ionic-strength deionized water but may fail in chloride- or sulfate-containing solutions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis may not hold in high-ion-content chloride solutions, yet the falsification design includes 3.5 wt.% NaCl and the rule does not specify that failure in this excluded medium cannot falsify the mechanism.
